item.title: Optimal Control of Inkjet Printing
item.description:
Machine learning embodies great potential in many interdisciplinary applications. In this project, we aim to find the optimal printing parameter of inkjet printers using machine learning methods.

We developed sampling methods for the experimental design, and our collaborator at Boise State University produced product lines based on our parameters combination and took microscope images of those lines.

We then developed image processing algorithms to calculate features of the printed lines. Multiple models were trained and compared and we eventually used neural networks as surrogate models for printing quality prediction.

item.title: Racial Disparity in SpO2
item.description:
Prior study at Michigan Medicine shows that the oxygen saturation (SpO2) measurement produced by pulse oximeters is biased toward people of color.

In this project at the Michigan Center for Integrative Research in Critical Care, we assessed the quality of SpO2 derived from patient’s bedside monitors and compared them with the gold standard arterial blood gas (ABG) results to look for potential bias.

SpO2 values that are potentially generated from noisy photoplethysmography (PPG) signals may be inaccurate. In particular, we augmented the PhysioNet Cardiovascular Signal Toolbox to assess the quality of each beat, and therefore determine how trustworthy a particular SpO2 value is. We also designed post-processing pipelines to enforce stricter requirements for a beat to be considered acceptable.
